montu-mia.title: Montu Mia's System Design
montu-mia.description: System design as a story. Bengali-first, now in English too. 3,000+ subscribers, 30,000+ readers, 147 GitHub stars.
montu-mia.longDescription: A system design book published as a website and LinkedIn newsletter, explaining fundamentals through the story of Montu Mia trying to keep a video platform alive. Chapters cover scaling, load balancers, networking, caching, CDNs, and the trade-offs nobody puts on the first slide. The site is bilingual (Bengali default, English under /en), with automated email newsletters, dynamic OG images, and a Fumadocs/MDX reading experience.
features: Story-driven system design chapters in Bengali and English
Automated email newsletter delivery via AWS SES
Dynamic OG image generation for social sharing
Documentation-style reading site with dark/light themes
challenges: Building an automated newsletter pipeline with AWS SES and React Email
Generating dynamic Open Graph images for each chapter
Keeping tone, humor, and character intact when translating with LLMs — then editing by hand
Making a documentation site feel like a book
impact: 3,000+ subscribers across email and LinkedIn
30,000+ readers and 100,000+ page views
147 GitHub stars for a Bengali-first educational project
English translation underway so the stories can travel further

trak.title: trak.sh
trak.description: Per-issue link analytics for newsletter writers. See which stories in a send actually got clicks — plus file drops with expiring links.
trak.longDescription: I write a newsletter. After every issue I wanted to know which stories actually landed — not which individual URL got a click, but which piece of the issue pulled weight. No shortener answered that, so I built one. trak.sh is a link analytics product with campaign grouping, a generous free tier, a REST API, and Drops for sharing private files with expiring download links. I use it every week on Montu Mia.
features: Per-issue / per-campaign link analytics for newsletters
No-signup shortening on the free tier
Drops: private file sharing with expiring download links
REST API, UTM presets, tags, QR codes, and public stats pages
Custom domains and CSV export on Pro
challenges: Designing analytics around issues and campaigns instead of isolated URLs
Shipping a usable free tier without making the product feel unfinished
Adding private file sharing (Drops) on top of a link-shortener core
impact: In production and used weekly on my own newsletter
Free forever plan plus a $6/month Pro tier

type-win.title: type.win
type-win.description: A retro typing arcade — Word Fall, Type Race, and a daily quote. Type fast. Type furious.
type-win.longDescription: type.win is an arcade-style typing game I built because most typing tests feel like forms. Word Fall rains words from the sky. Type Race is a WPM race against other people. There's a daily quote everyone shares. Keyboard-first, slightly ridiculous, best on a desktop.
features: Word Fall — type incoming words to survive
Type Race — live WPM races against other people
Daily quote — one shared run every UTC day
Keyboard-first arcade UI with leaderboards and profiles
challenges: Making a typing game feel like an arcade cabinet instead of a test
Building real-time races that stay fair and snappy
impact: A public typing arcade at type.win

ramble.title: Ramble
ramble.description: Your network, pooled-in. Search who-knows-what, transcribe meetings, and follow up on commitments with AI.
ramble.longDescription: Ramble is a private network-intelligence product. It builds dossiers from people you already know, lets you chat over that data, transcribes meetings, pulls out overheard commitments, and helps you actually follow up. The public pitch is 'who-knows-what'; the daily use is not losing the thread after a call.
features: RAG over your own contacts, notes, and conversations
Private dossiers for people in your network
challenges: Searching a private network without leaking it
Document conversations and summaries across multiple LLMs
Real-time collaborative editing with PlateJS and PubNub
Making meeting follow-ups feel automatic instead of like another app to maintain
impact: In production at ramble.ai as a network-intelligence product
Used for both meeting follow-up and 'who should I ask' search

claudebar.title: ClaudeBar
claudebar.description: A macOS menubar app that shows Claude Code usage, stats, and model breakdown at a glance.
claudebar.longDescription: ClaudeBar lives in the Mac menu bar and tells you how you've been using Claude Code — usage, stats, and which models you've been burning. I also published the menubar skill behind it: a Claude Code skill for spinning up single-file SwiftUI menubar apps.
features: Menu bar usage stats for Claude Code
Companion Claude Code skill for single-file menubar apps
challenges: Packing useful usage stats into a menubar without turning it into another dashboard
Turning the pattern into a reusable Claude Code skill
impact: A tiny tool I actually glance at while working
The menubar skill is published for other people to reuse

avro-silicon.title: Avro Silicon
avro-silicon.description: Avro phonetic keyboard modernized for Apple Silicon Macs after macOS warned the original would break.
avro-silicon.longDescription: I type Bengali in Avro every day. The macOS build hadn't been updated in years, didn't support Apple Silicon, and the system started warning it would die. I don't write Objective-C or InputMethodKit for a living — I teamed up with Claude Code, rebuilt it for arm64, ripped out legacy dependencies, and fixed a suggestion-accumulation bug that made typing lag. I didn't dump an AI-heavy PR on the original maintainer. The fork builds from source today.
features: Unicode normalization, expanded tests, and CI
challenges: Modernizing a legacy Objective-C input method without breaking daily typing
Replacing CocoaPods, RegexKitLite, and FMDB with system frameworks
Being honest about AI-generated code instead of dumping it on an upstream maintainer
impact: Keeps Bengali phonetic typing alive on M-series Macs
Public fork with build instructions while signing/notarization is still an open ask

vocables.title: Vocables
vocables.description: AI-powered vocabulary practice for IELTS, GRE, TOEFL, and SAT — suggestions, quizzes, and a word collection you actually review.
vocables.longDescription: Vocables is a vibe-coded vocabulary product for exam prep. It suggests words at your level, quizzes you, and lets you save and review a personal collection. Built with Next.js, Clerk, Polar, and the Vercel AI SDK.
features: AI word suggestions tailored to level and exam
IELTS, GRE, TOEFL, and SAT focus
challenges: Making vocab practice feel like a product instead of a flashcard dump
Wiring AI suggestions to a specific exam goal
impact: A live vocabulary product at vocables.xyz

profreach.title: Profreach
profreach.description: A professor outreach tracker for students applying to higher studies.
profreach.longDescription: Profreach is a small tool for a painful process: finding professors, writing to them, and not losing track of who you emailed three weeks ago. I built it because the spreadsheet version of this always falls apart.
challenges: Keeping outreach state simple enough that someone will actually use it
Tracking many parallel conversations without turning into a CRM
impact: A working outreach tracker at profreach.shakirul.dev

coterm.title: Coterm
coterm.description: Copilot for your terminal — natural language to CLI commands, built with Rust, Vercel edge functions, and OpenAI.
coterm.longDescription: Coterm sits between 'I know what I want' and 'I forgot the flags'. Describe the task in English, get a command, revise it, and run it with one key. Built in Rust with a Vercel edge function in front of OpenAI, plus guards for commands that can ruin your week.
features: Natural language to CLI command generation
challenges: Generating CLI commands from natural language without being reckless
Revising a generated command in-place
Running a command with one key press after confirmation
Keeping the OpenAI call on a Vercel edge function
impact: A learning tool for junior developers who freeze at the prompt
Public releases on GitHub

resume.title: Re:sume
resume.description: AI resume builder with PDF generation and OpenAI content enhancement.
resume.longDescription: Re:sume was an AI-powered resume builder: create a resume, store versions, enhance the writing with GPT, and export a PDF. Built at Re:cruit as a full-stack Next.js app on PostgreSQL and Prisma.
features: AI-powered content enhancement with OpenAI GPT
challenges: Prompting for resume content that doesn't sound like a robot wrote it
PDF layout that survives other people's life stories
A simple enough editor that people finish a resume
impact: Helped users create professional resumes

bochon.title: Bochon
bochon.description: Bengali speech-to-text model comparison platform, built for Bengali.AI.
bochon.longDescription: Bochon is a performance dashboard for Bengali.AI to show and compare Bengali speech-to-text models. Analytics, benchmarks, and interactive demos so researchers can see which ASR actually works.
challenges: Real-time audio processing in the browser
Visualizing model performance without lying with charts
A layout that still works when the data is messy
impact: Showcased Bengali ASR model capabilities
Made model comparison less of a spreadsheet
Contributed to Bengali.AI research tooling
